title: SLD resolution for definite Horn programs
summary: Resolve selected Horn goals against fresh program clauses, track computed answers, and prove completeness from finite least-model proof trees.
abstract: A rule for addition can answer a request for an unknown summand by replacing it with a simpler request. SLD resolution makes this backward reasoning precise: select an atom, match it with the conclusion of a freshly renamed program clause, and apply the resulting substitution to the whole remaining goal. A finite successful derivation gives an answer whose instance of the original query holds in every model of the program. Conversely, finite proof trees in the least term model produce a successful derivation for any fixed rule for selecting goal atoms, and every correct ground answer is an instance of some computed answer. Fresh variables and chronological substitution composition are essential to this correspondence. Breadth-first search can find the finite proof, while depth-first execution may remain forever on a recursive branch even when a one-step proof is available.

based_on.title: Logic for Computer Science: Foundations of Automatic Theorem Proving (corrected Dover second edition, June 2015)
based_on.pages: Chapter 9, §9.4, pp. 411–415: Definitions 9.4.1–9.4.2, Lemma 9.4.1 and Theorem 9.4.1
